title: BRICS Trade Union Forum 2026: the Hyderabad Declaration
author: Editorial Desk
summary: BMS hosted the 15th BRICS Trade Union Forum Summit from 14 to 16 July 2026.
body:
*Photo: 15th BRICS Trade Union Forum Summit, Hyderabad, July 2026*

From **14 to 16 July 2026**, the Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh hosted the **15th BRICS Trade Union Forum (TUF) Summit** in Hyderabad. According to BMS's report, the summit concluded on a historic note with the unanimous adoption of the **Hyderabad Declaration** for a **worker-centric global order**.

## What a TUF Summit does

It brings national trade union leaders from the BRICS countries together to discuss common challenges and to present a joint document to the governments that make up BRICS.

## The significance for BMS

- India chairs BRICS in 2026, so BMS was the host organisation for the trade union track.
- It was an occasion to put forward the BMS view of a **human-centred and worker-centric** international economy.
- It strengthened ties with trade union centres across the Global South.

## Themes typical of such declarations

Social protection for all, fair transition in the face of new technology, decent work in the platform economy, protection of migrant workers and a just international trade order. The exact text is available from the BMS website.

## An old slogan on a world stage

Thengadi Ji's formulation, *Workers unite the world*, was proposed in the 1950s as an answer to class conflict. At Hyderabad it was heard in the setting of global cooperation.
